evals.prompt: I just fixed a race condition in the cache layer, please commit my changes with a proper message.
evals.expected_output: Agent writes a commit whose title is imperative, capitalized, without a trailing period (e.g., `Fix cache race condition`) and passes the "If applied, this commit will ___" test.

evals.prompt: Review these commit messages from my teammate: `refactor: extract parser module`, `Updated the docs`, `Fix payment retry bug.` Which ones are fine?
evals.expected_output: `Updated the docs` flagged for past tense; `Fix payment retry bug.` flagged for trailing period; `refactor: extract parser module` flagged as Conventional Commits style with suggested rewrite `Extract parser module`. The agent enforces the imperative convention uniformly instead of accepting non-conforming styles.

evals.prompt: Our last 50 commits all use Conventional Commits (`feat: ...`, `fix: ...`). We're switching to plain imperative style from now on. Commit my staged changes.
evals.expected_output: Agent does not copy the historical convention; it writes an imperative title (e.g., `Add retry logic`), capitalized, no trailing period, demonstrating uniform enforcement regardless of repository history.
